title: AXPY on one vector register
formula: o = float32(float32(2 * x) + y) over a contiguous float32 [1, 64]
study_for: The smallest complete A5 demo: one `@vf` body, three UB tensors, one `auto_sync()` scope. Read this first to see what the four files of a demo folder are for before opening anything larger.

A `Reg` is a whole 64-lane vector register, not a scalar: `xr <<= x_ub[0]` loads the entire row and `muls`/`add` write one register each. The kernel has no loop because the shape is exactly one register wide.

Bitwise comparison is a claim about the arithmetic, not a default: multiplying by exactly 2.0 and adding in float32 is what the independent Torch reference also does, with no reduction and no fusion, so any difference is a defect.
do_not_copy_when: You need more than one core. This kernel has no partitioning: every lane of the output belongs to one vector core, and a second core would race.
Your shape is not exactly 64 lanes. There is no tail handling here — [1, 63] and [1, 65] are both wrong, not slow.
